components: Cache stampede: requests a cached item
Cache stampede: routes by key and version
Cache stampede: stores value and expiry
Cache stampede: tracks TTL and refill ownership
links: look up ownership in Freshness index

steps: A popular key expires while many clients are active.
Concurrent requests all observe the miss.
A per-key lock or shared promise elects one loader while peers wait or use stale data.
One source result refills the cache and releases all waiters.

lesson.scenario: Hundreds of requests hit an expired recommendation key and a single-flight lock limits source refill.
entities: Allows one refill owner per key
Serves bounded stale data to waiters

steps.title: Popular key valid
steps.narration: Version 31 has ten seconds left on its TTL.
steps.outcome: Normal traffic is absorbed by the cache.
steps.invariant: A hot key concentrates refill risk at one expiry boundary.

steps.title: Simultaneous expiry
steps.narration: The key expires as 500 requests arrive together.
steps.outcome: Without coordination, every miss could query the source.
steps.invariant: Expiry jitter reduces synchronization but does not eliminate refill races.

steps.title: One refill owner
steps.narration: One requester acquires the single-flight gate; 499 become waiters.
steps.outcome: Source fan-out is bounded to one query.
steps.invariant: The refill lock needs a timeout so a failed owner cannot block the key indefinitely.

steps.title: Stale while revalidate
steps.narration: Waiters receive bounded-stale version 31 while version 32 is computed.
steps.outcome: Latency and source load remain bounded during refill.
steps.invariant: Stale serving is safe only for data with an explicit acceptable-staleness policy.

steps.title: Fresh value published
steps.narration: The owner stores version 32 and releases the gate.
steps.outcome: Traffic returns to cache hits with a jittered expiry.
steps.invariant: Only a successfully published fresh value completes the refill generation.
